**Commentary on Surah an-Nasr (Surah 110)**

[[In M: "Tafsir Surat an-Nasr".]]

It is a Madani surah.

It has already been mentioned that it equals a quarter of the Qur'an, and that "Idha zulzilat" (Surah 99) equals a quarter of the Qur'an.

An-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ja'far informed us, from Abu al-'Umays (ḥ). And Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, Abu al-'Umays related to us, from 'Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl [[In A: "Sahl".]], from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "O son of 'Utba, do you know the last surah of the Qur'an to be revealed?" I said: "Yes, *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*." He said: "You are right." [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11713), and Muslim in his Sahih no. (3024) by way of Ja'far ibn 'Awn.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar and al-Bayhaqi narrated, from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi [[In A: "al-Zubayri".]], from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: This surah, *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and he understood that it signified the farewell. So he ordered his she-camel al-Qaswa' to be saddled, then he stood and addressed the people, and he mentioned his well-known sermon. [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (5/152), and Musa ibn 'Ubayda is weak.]]

Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, al-Asfati related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam related to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Fatima [[In A: "Fatima his daughter".]] and said: "Indeed, my soul has been announced to me." She wept, then she laughed. She said: "He told me that his soul had been announced to him, so I wept. Then he said: 'Be patient, for you are the first of my family to join me,' so I laughed." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwa lil-Bayhaqi (7/167).]]

An-Nasa'i has also narrated it, as will come later, without mention of Fatima.

*In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.*

* *

al-Bukhari said: Musa ibn Isma'il related to us, Abu 'Awana related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar used to bring me in with the elders of Badr. Some of them felt something in their hearts and said: "Why does he admit this one with us, when we have sons like him?" 'Umar said: "He is among those whom you know." So one day he called them and admitted him with them. I did not think that he had called me among them that day except to show them. He said: "What do you say about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*?" Some of them said: "We were commanded to praise Allah and seek His forgiveness when He gives us victory and opens (lands) for us." Some of them remained silent and said nothing. Then he said to me: "Is that what you say, O Ibn 'Abbas?" I said: "No." He said: "What do you say?" I said: "It is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which Allah informed him of." He said: "*Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* is the sign of your appointed time, *so glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance*." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I know of it nothing more than what you say." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4970).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated, from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Mihran, from al-Thawri, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, a similar account or close to it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/215).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, 'Ata' related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My soul has been announced to me," meaning that he would be taken in that year. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (1/217).]]

Al-'Awfi narrated, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it. Likewise said Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Dahhak, and others: it is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which was announced to him.

Ibn Jarir said: Isma'il ibn Musa related to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Isa al-Hanafi [[In A: "al-Thaqafi".]] related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Hazim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Madina, he said: "Allahu Akbar! Allahu Akbar! The victory of Allah has come, and the Fath has come, the people of Yemen have come." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the people of Yemen?" He said: "A people whose hearts are tender and whose natures are gentle. Faith is Yamani, understanding is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/215).]]

Then he narrated it from Ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from 'Ikrima, as a mursal report.

al-Tabarani said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us, Abu Kamil al-Jahdari related to us, Abu 'Awana related to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, through to the end of the surah, the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him the moment it was revealed. He said: So he strove harder than he ever had in matters of the Hereafter. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said after that: "The Fath has come, and the victory of Allah has come, and the people of Yemen have come." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the people of Yemen?" He said: "A people whose hearts are tender, whose hearts are gentle; faith is Yamani, and understanding is Yamani." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/328).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ knew that his soul had been announced to him. So it was said: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, the whole surah. [[Al-Musnad (1/344).]]

Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, that 'Umar asked Ibn 'Abbas about this verse: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*. He said: When it was revealed, the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him. [[Al-Musnad (1/356).]]

al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Waki'i related to us, my father related to us, Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, from Abu al-'Umays, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last surah to be revealed in its entirety from the Qur'an was *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/369).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'ba related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Abu al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i [[In A: "from Abu al-Bakhtari, from al-Ta'i".]], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: When this surah was revealed, *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it until he finished it, then he said: "The people are a group, and I and my companions are a group." He also said: "There is no hijra after the Fath, but there is jihad and intention." Marwan said to him: "You are lying." Zayd ibn Thabit and Rafi' ibn Khadij were with him, sitting with him on the couch. Abu Sa'id said: "If these two wished, they would narrate it to you, but this one fears that you will remove him from the leadership of his people, and this one fears that you will remove him from the zakat." Marwan raised the whip to strike him, but when they saw that, they both said: "He has spoken the truth." [[Al-Musnad (3/22).]]

Ahmad alone narrated it. What Marwan rejected from Abu Sa'id is not objectionable, for it has been established from the narration of Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Fath: "There is no hijra, but there is jihad and intention, and when you are called to march forth, then march forth." It was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their two Sahihs. [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (1834, 1349) and Sahih Muslim no. (1353).]]

As for what some of the Companions among 'Umar's companions explained, may Allah be pleased with them all, namely that He has commanded us, when Allah grants us the cities and fortresses (as conquest), to praise Allah, thank Him, and glorify Him, meaning to pray, and to seek His forgiveness, is a fine and sound meaning. And there is a witness to it established from the Prophet's ﷺ prayer on the day of the conquest of Makkah at the time of Duha, eight rak'as. Some said: it is the Duha prayer. It was answered that he did not consistently perform it, so how did he pray it that day while he was a traveler who had not intended to stay in Makkah? For this reason he remained there until the end of Ramadan, about nineteen days, shortening the prayer and breaking his fast, he and the whole army, which numbered about ten thousand. These scholars said: it was rather the prayer of the conquest. They said: it is recommended for the commander of an army, when he conquers a city, to pray eight rak'as upon first entering it.

Thus did Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas on the day he conquered al-Mada'in. Then some said: he prays them all with one salam. The correct view is that he makes salam after every two rak'as, as found in Sunan Abi Dawud: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to make salam after every two rak'as on the day of the conquest.

As for what Ibn 'Abbas and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, explained, that in this surah the soul of the noble Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced [[In M: "his spirit".]], know that when you conquer Makkah, which is your town that expelled you, and people enter the religion of Allah in multitudes, then our concern with you in this world has ended. So prepare to come to us and to receive the delegations coming to us. The Hereafter is better for you than this world, and your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be content. For this reason He said: *So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance*.

An-Nasa'i said: 'Amr ibn Mansur informed us, Muhammad ibn Mahbub related to us, Abu 'Awana related to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, through to the end of the surah, was revealed, the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him at its revelation. So he began to strive harder than ever in matters of the Hereafter. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said after that: "The Fath has come, the victory of Allah has come, and the people of Yemen have come." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the people of Yemen?" He said: "A people whose hearts are tender, whose hearts are gentle; faith is Yamani, wisdom is Yamani, and understanding is Yamani." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11712).]]

al-Bukhari said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say in his bowing and prostration: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me," interpreting the Qur'an.

The rest of the group narrated it, except al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Mansur, by the same chain. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4968); Sahih Muslim no. (484); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (877); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11710); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (889).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: 'A'isha said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say toward the end of his affairs: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance." And he said: "Indeed my Lord informed me that I would see a sign among my nation, and He commanded me that when I see it, I should glorify Him with His praise and seek His forgiveness, for He is ever Accepting of repentance. I have seen it: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath, wa ra'aita al-nas yadkhuluna fi dini Allahi afwajan, fa-sabbih bi-hamdi rabbika wa-astaghfirhu innahu kana tawwaban*."

Muslim narrated it by way of Dawud, who is Ibn Abi Hind, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (6/35) and Sahih Muslim no. (484).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, Hafs narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Umm Salama, who said: "In the final period of his life, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would neither stand nor sit, nor go nor come, without saying: 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi' (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him)." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you say 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi' so often, whether you go or come, stand or sit?" He said: "I have been commanded to do so." Then he recited: ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ to the end of the surah.

This hadith is gharib (rare). We have already compiled the hadiths about the expiation of the assembly (kaffarat al-majlis), with all their chains and wordings, in a separate part, so it is not repeated here. (The hadiths on the expiation of the assembly and their chains were mentioned at the end of the tafsir of Surah al-Saffat.)

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubayda, from 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud), who said: When ﴿When there comes the help of Allah and the victory﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would frequently say, when he recited it and bowed (in ruku'): "Subhanaka Allahumma Rabbana wa bihamdika, Allahumma ighfir li innaka anta al-Tawwab al-Rahim" three times.

Ahmad alone narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Shu'ba, from Abu Ishaq, with the same wording.

The victory (al-fath) here is, without disagreement, the conquest of Makkah. The Arab tribes had been waiting to see the outcome of the conquest of Makkah before embracing Islam, saying: "If he prevails over his people, then he is a prophet." When Allah granted him Makkah, they entered the religion of Allah in throngs, and within two years the Arabian Peninsula was united in faith, and none remained among the Arab tribes except one who displayed Islam. To Allah belong praise and grace.

al-Bukhari related in his Sahih from 'Amr ibn Salama, who said: "When the conquest came, every people hastened to bring their Islam to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the tribes had been waiting to embrace Islam until the conquest of Makkah, saying: 'Leave him and his people; if he prevails over them, then he is a prophet.'" The hadith...[(Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4302)]. We have examined the Battle of the Conquest in our book al-Sira, so whoever wishes should refer to it there. To Allah belong praise and grace.

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiya ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, who said: Abu 'Ammar narrated to me, a neighbour of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, who said: I came back from a journey, and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah came to me and greeted me. I began telling him about the splintering of the people and what they had innovated, and Jabir began to weep. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed the people entered the religion of Allah in throngs, and they will leave it in throngs."

[End of the tafsir of Surah "Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath." To Allah belong praise and grace.]

**Commentary on Surah an-Nasr (Surah 110)**

[[In M: "Tafsir Surat an-Nasr".]]

It is a Madani surah.

It has already been mentioned that it equals a quarter of the Qur'an, and that "Idha zulzilat" (Surah 99) equals a quarter of the Qur'an.

An-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ja'far informed us, from Abu al-'Umays (ḥ). And Muhammad ibn Sulayman informed us: Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, Abu al-'Umays related to us, from 'Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl [[In A: "Sahl".]], from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "O son of 'Utba, do you know the last surah of the Qur'an to be revealed?" I said: "Yes, *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*." He said: "You are right." [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11713), and Muslim in his Sahih no. (3024) by way of Ja'far ibn 'Awn.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar and al-Bayhaqi narrated, from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi [[In A: "al-Zubayri".]], from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: This surah, *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and he understood that it signified the farewell. So he ordered his she-camel al-Qaswa' to be saddled, then he stood and addressed the people, and he mentioned his well-known sermon. [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (5/152), and Musa ibn 'Ubayda is weak.]]

Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, al-Asfati related to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman related to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam related to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Fatima [[In A: "Fatima his daughter".]] and said: "Indeed, my soul has been announced to me." She wept, then she laughed. She said: "He told me that his soul had been announced to him, so I wept. Then he said: 'Be patient, for you are the first of my family to join me,' so I laughed." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwa lil-Bayhaqi (7/167).]]

An-Nasa'i has also narrated it, as will come later, without mention of Fatima.

*In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.*

* *

al-Bukhari said: Musa ibn Isma'il related to us, Abu 'Awana related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Umar used to bring me in with the elders of Badr. Some of them felt something in their hearts and said: "Why does he admit this one with us, when we have sons like him?" 'Umar said: "He is among those whom you know." So one day he called them and admitted him with them. I did not think that he had called me among them that day except to show them. He said: "What do you say about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*?" Some of them said: "We were commanded to praise Allah and seek His forgiveness when He gives us victory and opens (lands) for us." Some of them remained silent and said nothing. Then he said to me: "Is that what you say, O Ibn 'Abbas?" I said: "No." He said: "What do you say?" I said: "It is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which Allah informed him of." He said: "*Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* is the sign of your appointed time, *so glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance*." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I know of it nothing more than what you say." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4970).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated, from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Mihran, from al-Thawri, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, a similar account or close to it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/215).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, 'Ata' related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My soul has been announced to me," meaning that he would be taken in that year. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (1/217).]]

Al-'Awfi narrated, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it. Likewise said Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Dahhak, and others: it is the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which was announced to him.

Ibn Jarir said: Isma'il ibn Musa related to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Isa al-Hanafi [[In A: "al-Thaqafi".]] related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Hazim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Madina, he said: "Allahu Akbar! Allahu Akbar! The victory of Allah has come, and the Fath has come, the people of Yemen have come." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the people of Yemen?" He said: "A people whose hearts are tender and whose natures are gentle. Faith is Yamani, understanding is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/215).]]

Then he narrated it from Ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from 'Ikrima, as a mursal report.

al-Tabarani said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us, Abu Kamil al-Jahdari related to us, Abu 'Awana related to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, through to the end of the surah, the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him the moment it was revealed. He said: So he strove harder than he ever had in matters of the Hereafter. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said after that: "The Fath has come, and the victory of Allah has come, and the people of Yemen have come." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the people of Yemen?" He said: "A people whose hearts are tender, whose hearts are gentle; faith is Yamani, and understanding is Yamani." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/328).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath* was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ knew that his soul had been announced to him. So it was said: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, the whole surah. [[Al-Musnad (1/344).]]

Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, that 'Umar asked Ibn 'Abbas about this verse: *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*. He said: When it was revealed, the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced to him. [[Al-Musnad (1/356).]]

al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Waki'i related to us, my father related to us, Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, from Abu al-'Umays, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last surah to be revealed in its entirety from the Qur'an was *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/369).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'ba related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Abu al-Bakhtari al-Ta'i [[In A: "from Abu al-Bakhtari, from al-Ta'i".]], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: When this surah was revealed, *Idha ja'a nasr Allah wal-fath*, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it until he finished it, then he said: "The people are a group, and I and my companions are a group." He also said: "There is no hijra after the Fath, but there is jihad and intention." Marwan said to him: "You are lying." Zayd ibn Thabit and Rafi' ibn Khadij were with him, sitting with him on the couch. Abu Sa'id said: "If these two wished, they would narrate it to you, but this one fears that you will remove him from the leadership of his people, and this one fears that you will remove him from the zakat." Marwan raised the whip to strike him, but when they saw that, they both said: "He has spoken the truth." [[Al-Musnad (3/22).]]

Ahmad alone narrated it. What Marwan rejected from Abu Sa'id is not objectionable, for it has been established from the narration of Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of the Fath: "There is no hijra, but there is jihad and intention, and when you are called to march forth, then march forth." It was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their two Sahihs. [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (1834, 1349) and Sahih Muslim no. (1353).]]

As for what some of the Companions among 'Umar's companions explained, may Allah be pleased with them all, namely that He has commanded us, when Allah grants us the cities and fortresses (as conquest), to praise Allah, thank Him, and glorify Him, meaning to pray, and to seek His forgiveness, is a fine and sound meaning. And there is a witness to it established from the Prophet's ﷺ prayer on the day of the conquest of Makkah at the time of Duha, eight rak'as. Some said: it is the Duha prayer. It was answered that he did not consistently perform it, so how did he pray it that day while he was a traveler who had not intended to stay in Makkah? For this reason he remained there until the end of Ramadan, about nineteen days, shortening the prayer and breaking his fast, he and the whole army, which numbered about ten thousand. These scholars said: it was rather the prayer of the conquest. They said: it is recommended for the commander of an army, when he conquers a city, to pray eight rak'as upon first entering it.

Thus did Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas on the day he conquered al-Mada'in. Then some said: he prays them all with one salam. The correct view is that he makes salam after every two rak'as, as found in Sunan Abi Dawud: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to make salam after every two rak'as on the day of the conquest.

As for what Ibn 'Abbas and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, explained, that in this surah the soul of the noble Messenger of Allah ﷺ was announced [[In M: "his spirit".]], know that when you conquer Makkah, which is your town that expelled you, and people enter the religion of Allah in multitudes, then our concern with you in this world has ended. So prepare to come to us and to receive the delegations coming to us. The Hereafter is better for you than this world, and your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be content. For this reason He said: *So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance*.
